note: RAGE (https://darths-rage.netlify.app/) is capture-class: a single-file three.js action game served by Netlify at the origin root. §0.4 fork-over-mirror was checked on 2026-10-13 — no public upstream repo exists (the page carries no github/gitlab/bitbucket reference; a GitHub search finds only unrelated projects), so the mirror stands. Derived pipeline: capture → pinned prettier 3.9.6 (module API, default options, single pass verified idempotent — never the CLI: it respects .gitignore and can silently echo its input) → the entry document's inline <script> becomes readable/index-inline-1.pretty.js and its two inline <style> blocks become readable/index-inline-2|3.pretty.css (every pretty provably NOT byte-identical to its capture block; readable/index-inline-map.json records each block's exact byte range + sha256). The inline script is a SINGLE top-level IIFE (`(() => { … })();`): statement-aligned slices src/index-inline-1-NN.js are cut at the IIFE body's top-level statement boundaries (~250-350 line windows; oversized single declarations stay whole) with an exact 2-line provenance header; the IIFE wrapper head/tail and body statements that are not standalone at module top level (the engine guard contains a top-level `return`) are skipped sections, indexed but never sliced. Every slice parses standalone under `node --input-type=module --check -` and round-trips byte-exact to its recorded readable line range. Stylesheet rule — the two inline <style> blocks are wholeFile sections, never sliced. Non-code payloads (MP3 audio, WebP images, favicon.ico and the twelve glTF model/geometry JSON payloads) are hashed notRendered records (bytes + sha256, no pretty pass). The CDN dependencies (nine jsdelivr three.js r147 scripts, the Google Fonts stylesheet) were never captured (socker precedent, PLAN §1) and have no derived layer; tools/capture.mjs --check lists them as external off-origin references. Identifiers in src/ are the bundle's own minified names — the rename campaign (PLAN §5) is recorded as an open task in README.md, not claimed here. Capture bytes are untouched by everything above; re-cut with `node tools/derive.mjs` after any capture refresh. `node tools/audit.js` is the gate.
